name: picoc
why: A tiny C interpreter that runs C scripts without compiling, a delightfully odd take on a language people assume must be compiled.

brief.what_it_is: picoc is described on its GitLab project page as a very small C interpreter. The brew description says it runs C scripts directly, without a separate compile step. I could not read the README, so I have not confirmed what input it accepts or what output it produces beyond running C source. The executable it installs is named picoc.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was visible. The project page gave no build, runtime, or configuration steps.
brief.standout: Per the brew description, it runs C without compiling, which is unusual for a language normally thought of as compiled. I could not verify the details from the README.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab page shows a creation date of June 04, 2018 and no last-release or last-commit date. The README body did not load, so there is no evidence of current activity.
brief.caveats: The README did not load. The GitLab project page returned only the title, the one-line description, and the creation date. The raw README URL returned HTTP 404, so the brief relies on the brew description and the one-line project summary. Licensing, platform support, and feature limits are unknown.
